cases.name: ladder-keeps-the-newest-of-each-day
cases.notes: §7 Retention: five revisions of a.md over three days (two on Jan 1, one on Jan 2, two on Jan 3). Under `keep_days 0`, `per_doc_max 0` and a one-rung ladder `after 0 days: one per day`, the plan at Jan 10 keeps the newest revision of each day (r_1, r_2 and the current r_4) and archives r_0 and r_3. `history_export { prune }` writes segment s_0 over commits 1..4 (c_0 and c_3 are wholly archived: their dispositions go, their block_changes go except each block's earliest row — c_0's rows are the mint rows and stay), squashes the two revisions (NULL root_tree/frontmatter_blob, `archive = s_0`) and sweeps exactly the bodies reachable from nothing else. `read_at` reconstructs r_0 and r_3 through the attached segment byte for byte; after `history_detach` the same read is `revision_archived` with no path (the segment is not recorded); `history_attach` brings it back. A following `gc` has nothing left to collect.

cases.name: overrides-by-glob
cases.notes: §7: two documents on the same schedule; the override `/projects/**` with `keep_days 36500` keeps every revision under `projects/`, while `attn/focus.md` is thinned by the base one-per-day ladder. The first matching override replaces the keys it names and nothing else.

cases.name: never-prunable-current-and-tombstone-pending-row-pins-nothing
cases.notes: §7 the never-prunable set (17.0): b.md is observed three times and then deleted (tombstoned at c_3; its last revision r_2 stays its `head`), a.md twice; the `exec` device records a `pending_materializations` row for a.md — the api path's intent, which only the observe runner cannot produce — naming a.md's CURRENT head r_4, its `file_hash`, and as `prior_hash` the bytes the engine last wrote there (r_3's rendered hash), as a 17.0 commit would. Under a one-per-year ladder at Jan 10, 2027 the plan keeps r_2 (the tombstoned document's last revision) and r_4 (a.md's head) and archives b.md's r_0 and r_1 AND a.md's r_3: through 16.x rule 2 of §7.1 pinned the revision a pending row named; since 17.0 the row renders from the current rows and names no revision, so nothing is pinned for it — the row survives the squash unchanged and its replay still works (§5.7).

sql: INSERT INTO pending_materializations (repo_id, path, kind, from_path, doc_id, head, rendered_hash, prior_hash, commit_id, created_at) SELECT 'rp_0', 'a.md', 'write', NULL, d.doc_id, d.head, d.file_hash, (SELECT rendered_hash FROM revisions WHERE rev_id = 'r_3'), r.commit_id, c.ts FROM docs d JOIN revisions r ON r.rev_id = d.head JOIN commits c ON c.commit_id = r.commit_id WHERE d.doc_id = 'd_1'

cases.name: crash-rule-reuses-an-unrecorded-segment
cases.notes: §7 the crash rule: an export WITHOUT `prune` writes s_0 and records nothing — exactly the state a crash between the two phases leaves. The next export with `prune` finds the complete, unrecorded segment whose revisions are all still live and finishes it (`reused: true`, the same id, no second mint) instead of writing a new file; a further export has nothing to archive.

cases.name: detached-segment-is-left-alone
cases.notes: §7: after an export with `prune` and a `history_detach`, the segment file is still under the archives directory but every revision it holds is archived — it is `detached`, not a crashed export, so a further export neither reuses nor refuses it (nothing to archive, `segment: null`), and the read stays `revision_archived` until it is attached again.

cases.name: squash-reclaims-only-the-unreachable
cases.notes: §7 GC after a squash: r_0 and r_1 share the heading and the first paragraph with the current r_2 (structural sharing), so archiving them reclaims only their own tree nodes and the paragraph bytes no live revision names; the shared blobs stay. The segment is self-contained all the same — it carries every blob its revisions reach, shared or not.
